Count Me as One

The Figure-Eight Knot, the Trefoil's Turn, and One Trace Ladder: Two Quadratics Behind Gluing, Monodromy and the A-Polynomial

Jeromie Beasley · 20 November 2026

Claude's version, written from Jeromie Beasley's research programme

AI-assisted. The research direction and the three working rules are the author's; Claude (Anthropic) was used for computation, Lean formalisation, drafting and the 3D figures. Every identity stated as a theorem below is machine-checked in Lean 4 in the accompanying repository figure-eight-anchors-lean.

Abstract

Two quadratics, \(z^2-z+1\) and \(z^2-z-1\), are the two factors of Thurston's gluing equation for the figure-eight knot complement on the symmetric slice \(z=w\). We follow each of them through the classical invariants of the two simplest knots and show that they account for all of the following at once. The first factor is the shape of the regular ideal tetrahedron, the condition for Riley's parabolic representation of the figure-eight knot group, and the characteristic polynomial of the monodromy of the trefoil, which therefore has order six. The second factor fails the regularity test by exactly one sign; its square is the characteristic polynomial of the figure-eight monodromy (the cat map), which is the figure-eight's Alexander polynomial. Used as meridian eigenvalues, the two branches are precisely the ramification points of the figure-eight \(A\)-polynomial: the golden branch on the slice \(L=+1\) and the regular branch on \(L=-1\), the two fixed slices of the amphichiral involution \(L\mapsto 1/L\). A single trace ladder \(t_{k+1}=Tt_k-t_{k-1}\) carries the trefoil (\(T=1\), periodic), the band edge (\(T=2\), where the two rails merge), the figure-eight (\(T=3\), reaching \(123=\varphi^{10}+\varphi^{-10}\) at the fifth rung) and the Apéry and Catalan transports (\(T=6\), reaching \(34\)). Chirality is kept as a proved invariant: the figure-eight has an explicit mirror certificate and the trefoil provably has none. Each ingredient is classical; the contribution is the single map that joins them, stated as eighty machine-checked theorems with eighty-two typed relations, each relation witnessed by a theorem, and eleven false controls rejected.

1. Three working rules

This paper is organised by three rules that govern how the author tests ideas.

  1. Anchor a broken example to established mathematics. The anchors here are Thurston's ideal triangulation of the figure-eight knot complement, Riley's parabolic representation, and the genus-one Seifert surfaces of the two simplest fibred knots.
  2. Keep a raw difference as a ruler or a weight; do not renormalise it away. The branch of the gluing equation that is discarded as non-geometric, and the defect by which a group relation fails, are both kept and measured.
  3. Preserve the chiral source of asymmetry. The handedness of the trefoil is kept as a proved invariant and not averaged out.

Every result is graded: C classical and cited, T a theorem checked in Lean here, R a reading that joins classical facts and is checked as an identity here, O open.

2. The symmetric slice of Thurston's gluing equation

The complement of the figure-eight knot is glued from two ideal tetrahedra whose shape parameters \(z,w\) must satisfy the edge equation C [1]

\[ z(z-1)\,w(w-1)=1. \]
Theorem 1 T Gluing.edge_symmetric_factor. In every commutative ring, on the slice \(z=w\), \[ z^2(z-1)^2-1=(z^2-z+1)(z^2-z-1). \] Proof. Write \(u=z^2-z\). Then \(z^2(z-1)^2-1=u^2-1=(u+1)(u-1)\).

So the slice has two branches. The first, \(z^2-z+1=0\), is solved by \(z=e^{\pm i\pi/3}\); the second, \(z^2-z-1=0\), by \(z=\varphi\) and \(z=-1/\varphi\), with \(\varphi=(1+\sqrt5)/2\).

Theorem 2 T regular_cycle_fixed, cycle_fixed_regular, golden_cycle. Let \(z\) lie in a commutative ring. Then \(z(1-z)=1\) if and only if \(z^2-z+1=0\). If \(z^2-z-1=0\), then \(z(1-z)=-1\).
Proof. \(z(1-z)-1=-(z^2-z+1)\) and \(z(1-z)+1=-(z^2-z-1)\).

The map \(z\mapsto 1/(1-z)\) permutes the three dihedral shape parameters of an ideal tetrahedron. A shape fixed by it has all three dihedral parameters equal: that is the regular tetrahedron. The first branch is exactly the regular one. The second branch closes the bare edge equation just as well, but the same test returns \(-1\) in place of \(+1\). That sign is the first kept difference of the paper, and it carries the rest of the argument.

Theorem 3 T regular_half, eis_edge, eis_edge_conj. On the regular branch each tetrahedron contributes \(z(z-1)=-1\), and two contribute \((-1)(-1)=1\). In the Eisenstein integers \(\mathbb Z[\omega]\), \(\omega^2=\omega-1\), the edge equation holds at \(z=w=\omega=e^{i\pi/3}\) and at its conjugate \(1-\omega=e^{-i\pi/3}\), the mirror structure.
Theorem 4 T no_integer_regular, no_integer_golden. Neither branch has an integer shape: \(n^2-n+1\neq0\) and \(n^2-n-1\neq0\) for every integer \(n\).
Proof. \(n(n-1)\ge0\) for every integer \(n\), which excludes \(n(n-1)=-1\); and \(n(n-1)\) is always even, which excludes \(n(n-1)=1\).

3. One polynomial in three places

3.1 Riley's representation

The figure-eight knot group has the presentation \(\langle a,b\mid wa=bw\rangle\) with \(w=a^{-1}bab^{-1}\). Riley [2] sends

\[ a\mapsto A=\begin{pmatrix}1&1\\0&1\end{pmatrix},\qquad b\mapsto B=\begin{pmatrix}1&0\\c&1\end{pmatrix}. \]
Theorem 5 T Riley.relation_defect, riley_iff_shape. In every commutative ring, with \(W=A^{-1}BAB^{-1}\) and \(p=c^2-c+1\), \[ WA-BW=\begin{pmatrix}0&p\\-cp&0\end{pmatrix}. \] Hence the relation holds if and only if \(c^2-c+1=0\).

The Riley polynomial of the figure-eight knot is the regular-tetrahedron polynomial C [2, 3]. Keeping the whole defect matrix, and not only the equation \(p=0\), is an instance of the second rule: away from the root, the failure of the relation is measured, and it is measured by the same quadratic. Both meridians are parabolic, \(\operatorname{tr}A=\operatorname{tr}B=2\), so they sit exactly on the band edge of Section 5.

3.2 The trefoil's monodromy

A genus-one fibred knot with Seifert matrix \(V\) has monodromy \(h=V^{-1}V^{T}\) on the homology of its fibre, and its Alexander polynomial is the characteristic polynomial of \(h\) C [4]. For the trefoil and the figure-eight we take

\[ V_{3_1}=\begin{pmatrix}-1&1\\0&-1\end{pmatrix},\qquad V_{4_1}=\begin{pmatrix}1&-1\\0&-1\end{pmatrix}. \]
Theorem 6 T Monodromy.h31_form, h31_charpoly, h31_cubed, h31_order6. \(h_{3_1}=\begin{pmatrix}0&1\\-1&1\end{pmatrix}\), with \(\operatorname{tr}h_{3_1}=1\), \(\det h_{3_1}=1\), and \[ h_{3_1}^2=h_{3_1}-I,\qquad h_{3_1}^3=-I,\qquad h_{3_1}^6=I. \]
Corollary 7 R. The monodromy of the trefoil, the Riley parameter of the figure-eight knot, and the shape of the regular ideal tetrahedron all satisfy \(z^2-z+1=0\). In particular the trefoil's monodromy, which is chiral, satisfies the polynomial from which the hyperbolic structure of the amphichiral figure-eight knot is built.

Each of the three facts is classical. The corollary records that they are one polynomial. It does not claim a map between the objects; it is the shared root \(e^{i\pi/3}\), a sixth root of unity, that appears in all three. The same sixfold structure appears in the author's Dirac Time programme [12], where on the unitary trefoil arc the longitude closes as \(\Lambda=-U^{-6}\), so that \(LM^{6}=-1\) on the meridian eigenline; here the homological monodromy closes as \(h^3=-I\), \(h^6=I\). Both are the \((2,3)\) torus-knot structure seen in two representations; the agreement of the sign \(-1\) is recorded as a structural reading only.

4. The kept difference: the golden branch squared

Theorem 8 T Monodromy.h41_cat, h41_charpoly, Ladder.golden_squared. \(h_{4_1}=\begin{pmatrix}2&1\\1&1\end{pmatrix}\), the cat map, with \(h_{4_1}^2=3h_{4_1}-I\). If \(z^2-z-1=0\) in a commutative ring, then \(x=z^2\) satisfies \[ x^2-3x+1=0, \] the characteristic polynomial of \(h_{4_1}\) and the Alexander polynomial of the figure-eight knot.
Proof. From \(z^2=z+1\): \(z^4=(z+1)^2=z^2+2z+1=3z+2\), so \(z^4-3z^2+1=3z+2-3z-3+1=0\).

So the branch that fails the regularity test by a sign is not waste. Squared, it is the stretch of the figure-eight monodromy, \(\lambda_+=\varphi^2\). The corresponding statement for the regular branch is that \(z^2\) is a primitive cube root of unity (Ladder.regular_squared): squaring keeps the regular branch on the circle and sends the golden branch off it.

Theorem 9 T Monodromy.h41_trace5, Ladder.fig8_fifth. \(\operatorname{tr}h_{4_1}^5=123\). Equivalently, if \(x^2-3x+1=0\) then \(x^5+(3-x)^5=123=\varphi^{10}+\varphi^{-10}\).

The number \(123\) reappears outside knot theory. The convergence ratio of the \(\pi\) continued fraction of the Ramanujan Machine Challenge, Question 1, is \((123+55\sqrt5)/2=\varphi^{10}\) C [10]; its trace is \(123\). This is recorded as a link, not proved here.

5. One trace ladder

Theorem 10 T Ladder.ladder_law. In every commutative ring, if \(x+y=T\) and \(xy=1\), then \(x^k+y^k=t_k\) for all \(k\ge0\), where \(t_0=2\), \(t_1=T\) and \(t_{k+1}=Tt_k-t_{k-1}\).
Proof. \(x^{k+2}+y^{k+2}=(x+y)(x^{k+1}+y^{k+1})-xy(x^k+y^k)\); induct on \(k\).

The ladder has three regimes. For \(|T|<2\) the two rails \(\lambda_\pm=(T\pm\sqrt{T^2-4})/2\) are complex conjugates on the unit circle and the ladder rotates (the band). For \(|T|>2\) they are real and the ladder stretches (the gap). At \(|T|=2\) the two rails coincide (band_edge_merge): this is the exceptional point between the regimes. In the author's rail-angle variables [13] the angle \(\psi\) between the two rails in companion coordinates satisfies \(T=2\sec\psi\), the rails are \(\sec\psi\pm\tan\psi\), and the stretch per step is \(\log\lambda_+=\operatorname{gd}^{-1}(\psi)\), the inverse Gudermannian.

Proposition 11 T trefoil_ladder, fig8_ladder, sqrt2_ladder.
  • \(T=1\) (trefoil): \(2,1,-1,-2,-1,1,2,\dots\), periodic with period \(6\); rotation \(60^\circ\) per step.
  • \(T=3\) (figure-eight): \(2,3,7,18,47,123,322,\dots\); \(\sec\psi=3/2\), \(\psi=48.19^\circ\), \(\lambda_+=\varphi^2\).
  • \(T=6\): \(2,6,34,198,\dots\); \(\lambda_+=(1+\sqrt2)^2\).

The rung \(34\) of the \(T=6\) ladder is the trace of \((1+\sqrt2)^4=17+12\sqrt2\), the dominant root of Apéry's \(\zeta(3)\) recurrence, whose limiting polynomial is \(\lambda^2-34\lambda+1\) C [9]. The Catalan transport of the Ramanujan Challenge, Problem 2.5, carries it verbatim:

Theorem 12 T catalan_contains_apery, antipalindromic_rest, saddle_unit, apery_middle.
  1. \(\lambda^3-35\lambda^2+35\lambda-1=(\lambda-1)(\lambda^2-34\lambda+1)\); more generally every \(\lambda^3-a\lambda^2+a\lambda-1\) equals \((\lambda-1)(\lambda^2-(a-1)\lambda+1)\), so the rest mode \(\lambda=1\) is forced.
  2. If \(t^2+2t-1=0\), then \(t^4(t+2)^4=1\) and \(t^4+(t+2)^4=34\).
  3. \(34n^3+51n^2+27n+5=(2n+1)(17n^2+17n+5)\).

Item 2 is the shared saddle quadratic of Beukers' integral for Apéry's \(\zeta(3)\) and of the official proof of Problem 2.5; its root is \(\sqrt2-1\) and \(t+2=1/t\). The trefoil, the figure-eight, and the two arithmetic transports therefore sit on one ladder, at \(T=1\), \(3\) and \(6\to34\), on the two sides of the band edge.

6. The branches are branch points of the A-polynomial

The \(A\)-polynomial of the figure-eight knot is C [5, 6]

\[ A(L,M)=M^4L^2+b(M)\,L+M^4,\qquad b(M)=-1+M^2+2M^4+M^6-M^8. \]
Theorem 13 T APoly.palindromic. If \(L\,L'=1\) then \(L^2A(L',M)=A(L,M)\): \(A\) is palindromic in \(L\).

The involution \(L\mapsto1/L\) is the amphichiral symmetry of the figure-eight knot on its character curve [6]; its fixed slices are \(L=+1\) and \(L=-1\). The author's earlier paper on this curve [14] showed that this palindromicity is why every singular point lying on \(L=\pm1\) has a tangent cone aligned with the meridian and longitude axes.

Theorem 14 T APoly.disc_split, plus_factor, minus_factor. With \(a=M^4\) and \(x=M^2\), \[ b^2-4a^2=(b+2a)(b-2a),\quad b+2a=-(x+1)^2(x^2-3x+1),\quad b-2a=-(x-1)^2(x^2+x+1). \]

On \(L=1\) both \(A\) and \(\partial_LA\) equal \(b+2a\); on \(L=-1\) they are \(\mp(b-2a)\). The double factors \((x\pm1)^2\) give the nodes; the simple factors give the four ramification points, in agreement with [6]. The simple factors are exactly the two squared branches of Section 4:

Theorem 15 T APoly.golden_ramifies, regular_ramifies. In every commutative ring: if \(z^2-z-1=0\) then \(A(1,z)=0\) and \(\partial_LA(1,z)=0\); if \(z^2-z+1=0\) then \(A(-1,z)=0\) and \(\partial_LA(-1,z)=0\). Used as a meridian eigenvalue \(M=z\), the golden shape is a ramification point of the figure-eight \(A\)-polynomial on \(L=+1\), and the regular shape is one on \(L=-1\).

The roots \(x^2-3x+1=0\) on \(L=1\) are the roots of the Alexander polynomial, where the classical theory of Burde and de Rham places the reducible non-abelian representations C [7, 8]. Thurston's two shape branches, squared, are therefore the two families of special points of the character curve: the Alexander roots on the fixed slice \(L=+1\) and the cube roots of unity on the fixed slice \(L=-1\).

Remark 16 O. Why the flat (real-shaped) branch of the symmetric gluing slice lands on the Alexander roots is not derived here. A natural conjecture is that real shape solutions of the slice correspond to the reducible non-abelian representations at \(M^2\) a root of \(\Delta_{4_1}\). This is untested.

7. Chirality on the Seifert form

Theorem 17 T Chirality.amphichiral_41. With \(P=\begin{pmatrix}-1&-1\\2&1\end{pmatrix}\), \(\det P=1\), one has \(P^{T}V_{4_1}P=-V_{4_1}^{T}\), the Seifert matrix of the mirror image. The figure-eight knot is its own mirror image on its Seifert form.
Theorem 18 T Chirality.S31_form, chiral_31, chiral_31_basic. For every unimodular integer \(P\), \(P^{T}V_{3_1}P\neq-V_{3_1}^{T}\). The trefoil is chiral.
Proof. Let \(S=V_{3_1}+V_{3_1}^{T}=\begin{pmatrix}-2&1\\1&-2\end{pmatrix}\). For every nonzero integer vector \((x,y)\), \[ (x,y)S(x,y)^{T}=-2(x^2-xy+y^2)<0,\qquad 4(x^2-xy+y^2)=(2x-y)^2+3y^2. \] If \(P^TV_{3_1}P=-V_{3_1}^T\), then symmetrising gives \(P^TSP=-S\). The top-left entry of \(P^TSP\) is the form evaluated at the first column of \(P\), which is nonzero because \(\det P=\pm1\), so it is negative; the top-left entry of \(-S\) is \(+2\). Contradiction.

The figure-eight form \(V_{4_1}+V_{4_1}^T\) is indefinite (signature \(0\)), so a basis change can reach its negative; the trefoil form is negative definite (signature \(-2\)), so none can. The asymmetry is an invariant and is kept. The three central polynomial identifications above relate a chiral object (the trefoil's monodromy) to an amphichiral one (the figure-eight's geometry) without removing the chirality of either.

8. The relation graph and the harness

Every theorem of the repository is a node of a graph, tagged with the rule or rules it serves, and every connection stated in this paper is a typed edge. The edge types are same polynomial, same root, same value, square of, kept difference, contrast, mirror, boundary, ladder step, generalises, converse, evaluates in, proof step, anchor, external and analogy only. Each edge names the Lean theorem that witnesses it. External edges record links to the author's other work and to the literature and are not proved here; one edge is marked analogy-only and has no theorem behind it.

The verification harness runs, on every build:

  1. lake build of every module;
  2. an independent replay of every module in leanchecker;
  3. an axiom audit: every one of the 80 theorems uses only propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound, and 32 use no axioms at all;
  4. a source scan for sorry, admit, native_decide and axiom;
  5. a theorem inventory, which must equal 80;
  6. eleven false controls, each of which must be rejected by Lean proving the false statement false;
  7. the relation graph: every theorem must be a node with a rule tag and at least one edge, every edge end must be a theorem or a declared source, every witness must be an audited theorem, and a forged edge is passed through the same checker and must be rejected;
  8. SHA-256 hashes of every source file and of the graph.

All eight checks pass on Lean 4.34.1, core library only. The Lean source, the false controls and the harness are printed in full in the PDF edition.

9. Scope

Every identity stated as a theorem is exact and checked. The external links (Question 1's ratio, the Catalan and Apéry transports, the ramification points in the literature, the Dirac Time sixfold structure) are recorded and cited, not proved here. The corollary of Section 3 and the ramification reading of Section 6 join classical facts into one statement; they claim shared polynomials, not maps between the objects. The mechanism of Remark 16 is open. The point clouds in the plates are rendering samples of computed geometry and carry no density of anything physical.
